column4: Visit note | 2025-09-13 10:30 AM | Dr. Tahmina Begum, Dermatology | Patient: Nayeem Islam, 53, male. Mr. Islam presents with itchy dry patches on his elbows and knees that cause him to scratch at night, with symptoms worse in winter. He is a graphic designer and mentions his condition flared during the dry winter in Mohammadpur. He reports no other systemic complaints and has no known comorbidity. Examination reveals an affected area about 11 cm across, alongside BP 121/80 mmHg, pulse 72 bpm, and weight 86 kg. The surrounding skin is dry with mild excoriation marks. Assessment: Atopic eczema. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no medicine needed at this stage, and no new medicine was prescribed today. He was advised to use a mild soap, avoid hot baths, and wear cotton clothes. Follow-up in 2 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-09-13 03:00 PM | Dr. Nusrat Jahan, General Medicine | Patient: Tariq Mondal, 44, male. Mr. Mondal reports feeling extremely tired and looking pale, getting breathless on the stairs, and noticing brittle nails, along with a craving to chew ice and a sore smooth tongue. He works as a beautician and states his symptoms worsened after a long spell of poor meals while living alone in Rajshahi. He has no chronic comorbidity and denies chest pain or palpitations. On examination: haemoglobin 8.8 g/dL, BP 120/73 mmHg, pulse 68 bpm, and weight 67 kg. Conjunctivae are pale and mucosal pallor is noted. Assessment: Iron deficiency anaemia. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment: a complete blood count and serum ferritin; no new medicine was prescribed. He was advised to eat more lentils, spinach, liver, and eggs, and avoid tea within an hour of meals. Follow-up after the test results are ready.

Visit note | 2025-09-14 03:30 PM | Dr. Anisur Rahman, Ophthalmology | Patient: Arafat Hossain, 70, male. Mr. Hossain states his eyes feel dry and irritated after long hours of screen time, noting that symptoms are worse in air conditioning. He works as a homemaker and shares that his discomfort began after long gaming sessions at home in Gulshan. He reports no visual loss, discharge, or eye pain and has no comorbidity. Examination shows a tear break-up time 4 seconds, BP 124/74 mmHg, pulse 82 bpm, and weight 90 kg. Conjunctivae are clear with mild dryness signs. Assessment: Dry eye syndrome. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no medicine needed at this stage, and no new medicine was prescribed today. He was advised to look away from the screen every 20 minutes, blink often, and use a humidifier. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-09-15 09:00 AM | Dr. Rokeya Khatun, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Tania Hossain, 26, female. Ms. Hossain reports noticeable weight gain and extra hair on her face. She works as a journalist and mentions her symptoms were noticed after a friend in Shyamoli suggested testing. She has a history of Bronchial asthma but no other systemic complaints. On examination: BMI 31.5, BP 131/81 mmHg, pulse 73 bpm, and weight 47 kg. Chest examination reveals clear breath sounds with no wheeze. Assessment: Polycystic ovary syndrome. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment: a pelvic ultrasound and hormone profile; no new medicine was prescribed. She was advised to aim for 5% weight loss, exercise 150 minutes a week, and reduce sugary drinks. Follow-up after the test results are ready.

Visit note | 2025-09-16 10:00 AM | Dr. Sadia Islam, Dermatology | Patient: Ziaur Molla, 31, male. Mr. Molla complains of itchy dry patches on the elbows and knees that feel worse in winter. He works as a journalist and states his condition flared during the dry winter in Sylhet. He has no comorbid illnesses and denies joint pain or fever. On examination: affected area about 4 cm across, BP 127/70 mmHg, pulse 71 bpm, and weight 51 kg. Skin shows localized lichenification over the extensor surfaces. Assessment: Atopic eczema. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment: no tests; no new medicine was prescribed today. He was advised to use a mild soap, avoid hot baths, and wear cotton clothes. Follow-up after the test results are ready.
